seen_animation: Frame 1: a wide flat field below a horizon with two grey trees; about forty birds lie on the ground as short flattened black arcs in rows, with a wavy water line at the bottom. Frames 2-4: birds at the left and centre open into the doodle's M shapes and lift off in small stacked groups. Frames 5-8: more groups rise above the horizon and the view tilts upward, so the horizon and trees move down the frame; a straggling group stays low in the centre. Frames 9-12: almost all groups are in the air in the upper half; the horizon sits in the lower third with the two trees; one last group rises from the bottom middle. Frames 13-16: the whole flock is spread across the upper two-thirds of the sky above a low horizon with two trees, drifting slightly.
seen_film: Frame 1: a large flock of dark geese sits on a brown reed field in front of bare trees, with a pale water strip at the bottom. Frames 2-4: geese at the left and centre start flapping and lifting. Frames 5-8: most of the flock is airborne in front of the trees and the camera tilts up, pushing the field and water down and out of frame. Frames 9-12: the flock fills the sky above a low brown field and bushes; a few geese still rise from the bottom. Frames 13-16: the camera holds on a dense flock flying across the upper two-thirds of the frame with bare trees behind and the field in the bottom quarter.
named_subject: a flock of geese taking off from a field, drawn as the doodle's groups of one large M bird over three small m birds
evidence: Judged from still frames only, not playback. Take-off begins in the same place and time: e.png 3-8 show left and centre birds opening into M shapes as f.png 3-8 show the left and centre geese lifting. The upward camera tilt matches: the horizon moves from about 45% down the frame (e.png 1) to about 60% (e.png 17) to about 70% (e.png 33), as the film's field moves down over f.png 1-40. The straggling group that rises from the bottom centre in e.png 17-38 corresponds to the late risers in f.png 25-40. e.png 41-56 hold a flock across the sky above a low horizon with two trees, matching f.png 41-56. g.png shows the tracked group climbing steadily upward from 1 to the top numbers with no reversal or gap. Consecutive frames in e.png rows 3-5 (17-40) show groups shifting a small amount per frame without pops or doubled drawings.
primary_gap: In e.png 41-56 the flock is sparser and evenly spaced in identical four-bird stacks, while f.png 41-56 show a dense, irregular mass of geese packed across the upper two-thirds of the frame.
closes_when: e.png 41-56 show more groups packed closer together and at varied spacing and heights so the sky area in the upper two-thirds is as filled as in f.png 41-56.
protect: The doodle's stroke habits (one large rounded M over three small angular m marks, thick black single lines); the grounded birds as flattened arcs that open into M shapes on take-off; the take-off order (left and centre first, a late group from bottom centre); the camera tilt that moves the horizon down at the film's rate; the steady upward path with no reversals; the plain grey line scenery with two trees.
identity_gap: The birds are the doodle's M and m marks, but they are repeated as near-identical four-bird stamps, so the late flock looks tiled rather than like the doodle's loose single grouping.
